critical_code_review_comments: server.py: seed_all runs inside app_context on import — good, and tolerates DB failure. Note: the WsgiToAsgi wrapper means every request goes through the asgi→wsgi bridge; fine for this scale but adds latency.
activity.log() swallows all exceptions silently. Recommend at least logging.warning on failure so DB outages are debuggable.

profile.change_password validates `current and new and current == new` — but this check runs AFTER verify_password, so a wrong-current-with-same-as-current pw could still hit; harmless in practice because verify_password will fail first. Consider re-ordering to reject same-as-current unconditionally.

students._next_student_id sorts by string student_id descending, which works while all IDs are STU-0xx but will break sort order past STU-099 → STU-100 vs STU-099 (STU-099 > STU-100 lexicographically). Consider padding or a separate counter collection before scaling past 99 students.

courses._validate: message says 'Course code must be 3–10 chars, letters/digits only' but the regex requires uppercase specifically. The form's style=text-transform:uppercase is cosmetic; server-side .upper() handles it, so the error text is slightly misleading (a user typing 'ab' hits the length rule first, but 'abc' would pass because it's upper()'d — no bug, just imprecise message).

admin.monitoring computes active_sessions from auth.login events in last 30m. Users who logged in >30m ago but are still using the site are excluded — reasonable, but 'active sessions' label may mislead. Consider renaming to 'Recent logins (30m)'.
student_form.html year select uses `student.year|int == y` — fine because seed stores year as int. If any legacy row stored year as string, `|int` filter still works.

dashboard.html: stat-users card links to /admin only for admins, else to /dashboard (self-link). This matches the review note but is a UX oddity — a plain user clicking the users card gets no navigation. Consider making it a non-anchor for non-admins.

No CSRF protection on POST forms (students/courses/profile). Since sessions are cookie-based with SameSite=Lax, cross-site attacks are limited, but adding Flask-WTF CSRF would be prudent for a phase-3 hardening.
server.py error handlers catch 500 but don't hide traceback in production. Since DEBUG isn't forced off, ensure FLASK_DEBUG=0 in prod.
